description: An autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease, most often affecting older adults.
causes: Autoantibodies directed against proteins at the basement membrane zone of the skin

appearance.general: Tense fluid-filled blisters arising on normal or urticated skin; widespread erosions may follow rupture.

warning_signs: Extensive blistering, dehydration, infection, or mucosal involvement requires medical evaluation.
doctor_discussion_points: Discuss new medicines, neurological history, and whether biopsy or immunofluorescence is needed.
